summary: Signed webhook provenance and deliverability sample for customer security assurance
description:
Issue summary:
FinTrust Bank requests a concrete deliverable demonstrating per-event provenance for our webhook SIEM export. They require: per-request Ed25519 signatures, sequence numbers and resume tokens, HMAC/MTLS alternative, deduplication token semantics, a short canonical JSON sample (3 contiguous events) with signed manifest and delivery receipts, and a small runbook showing how to validate signatures and perform replay protection verification.

Impact:
Customer security/compliance team needs artefacts to close an external audit. Without a signed sample and delivery proof the customer will block production data export to their SIEM, delaying onboarding and potentially impacting contract milestones.

Environment:
Production export to customer-managed SIEM via webhook (FinTrust staging endpoint in eu-west). Export config: push delivery, per-tenant topic, payload format: ndjson, claimed signature header: X-RW-SIGN, resume-token header: X-RW-RESUME.

Steps to reproduce / customer ask:
1) We need a 3-event contiguous sample (ordered by sequence) from prod with the following attached: event body (ndjson), per-event Ed25519 signature, canonical hash (SHA-256 hex), resume token for the batch, and a signed manifest listing event IDs and checksums.
2) Proof of delivery: webhook HTTP 2xx receipts with timestamp and remote IP, plus an acknowledgement HMAC if possible.
3) Documentation: exact header names, key rotation timing, signature verification snippet (Python/Go) and an example of deduplication logic using our resume-token semantics.
4) Security questionnaire snippet: list of KMS used for signing, key rotation cadence, who has access, and whether signatures are attested by HSM.

Logs / examples attached by customer in thread (see comments).
comments: 2026-03-05 09:12 - Ethan Rivers: Opened on behalf of FinTrust. Customer provided staging endpoint and example event IDs (evt-20260305-844, evt-20260305-845). Requested by their SOC team for audit window ending 2026-03-10.

2026-03-05 10:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Acknowledged request. Asked customer to confirm whether they prefer Ed25519 signatures in header or detached JWS, and whether MTLS is an acceptable alternative during evidence exchange.

2026-03-05 11:34 - FinTrust (Olivia Kane): Replied that Ed25519 in X-RW-SIGN header preferred; MTLS is acceptable as fallback. Requested immutable manifest with RFC3339 timestamps and explicit nonce per-batch.

2026-03-06 08:47 - SRE Oncall (Noah Chen): Investigating production export logs for the requested event range. Noted some prior signature mismatches in March related to rotation timing. Asked platform for rotation records for signing key v2.

2026-03-07 14:22 - Engineering (Ava Martinez): Confirmed we can produce signed samples. Need to verify private key location and whether signing is HSM-backed for this tenant. Created internal task INT-119390 to verify key attestation and rotation logs.

2026-03-08 09:30 - Support (Maya Patel): Sent temporary test harness (python) to customer to validate signatures; asked for sample webhook logs showing the signature header and raw body for evt-20260305-844.
2026-03-09 12:05 - FinTrust (Olivia Kane): Uploaded webhook logs and confirmed receipt of test harness. Also requested that receipts include TLS peer certificate fingerprint in the manifest.

2026-03-09 15:40 - SRE (Noah Chen): Found the events and produced preliminary signed bundle. Observed one event (evt-20260305-845) had a truncated body in the export pipeline; we've marked that for replay and will include corrected event in the manifest.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Signature mismatches seen previously were caused by misalignment between canonicalization rule in customers' verifier and our NDJSON newline normalization; 2) Key v2 rotation occurred at 2026-02-28 23:59 UTC and some in-flight signing used both v1 and v2; delivery receipts may lack explicit certificate fingerprints. Findings: Signed events located for requested window. One event truncated by delivery buffer limit; sequence integrity preserved via resume token. Internal task INT-119390 tracks key attestation and will confirm HSM provenance.
resolution: Workaround provided: SRE produced a signed sample bundle with three contiguous events (evt-20260305-843, evt-20260305-844, evt-20260305-846) along with a signed manifest (Ed25519) and server-side receipts showing 2xx responses and TLS peer fingerprint. We recommended customer validate using provided Python snippet which canonicalizes JSON by sorting keys and trimming trailing newlines. For production handoff, offered MTLS-backed delivery for the onboarding window to remove signature-rotation ambiguity. Follow-ups: INT-119390 to produce key rotation audit (due 2026-03-12), a small platform change LOG-2378 to emit X-RW-KEY-VERSION header on each webhook, and a customer-facing playbook page added to Confluence. Customer confirmed the sample satisfied initial audit checks and will update once final rotation attestation is complete.
